nodes.title: Training on a rented GPU is optional. Every model can also be trained on the laptop alone, and results are reproducible from a seed either way.

criteria: Given the same seed and data, when a model is trained twice on the same hardware, then the forecasts match within 1e-6.

nodes.title: At each rebalance, weights are set from return forecasts, volatility forecasts and the best S2 covariance estimate, all as of the rebalance date. The weights are long-only, fully invested and unlevered.

criteria: Given a rebalance date, when weights are built, then they satisfy PORT-01 and use only forecasts made with data up to that date.

nodes.title: A turnover limit is applied so costs do not dominate: one-way turnover is at most 50% per rebalance.

criteria: Given earlier and new target weights, when the trade is made, then one-way turnover is ≤ 50%.

nodes.title: A forecast portfolio "beats the classical portfolios" only if all of these hold, each tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction across all comparisons:

criteria: its after-cost Sharpe ratio is higher than every S2 portfolio's (null of equal Sharpe rejected);
its realized variance is lower than that of the risk parity, hierarchical risk parity and equal-weight portfolios (null of equal variance rejected);
against each minimum-variance portfolio, its realized variance is not significantly higher (null of equal variance not rejected in the "higher" direction).

nodes.title: The final verdict also needs the paper-trading result (PAPER-05), which can veto a holdout pass but cannot replace one.

criteria: Given a holdout pass and a paper-trading fail, when the verdict is recorded, then it is "does not beat".
Given a holdout fail and a paper-trading pass, when the verdict is recorded, then it is "does not beat".

nodes.title: The environment's state at day D holds only information as of D: surviving features, forecasts, recent returns and current weights.

criteria: Given the environment at D, when the state is inspected, then no value is dated after D.

nodes.title: The agent's action is a set of target weights that meet PORT-01. Trades are filled at D+1 under the cost model (EVAL-02).

criteria: Given any action, when it is applied, then the weights are non-negative and sum to 1, and the cost charged follows EVAL-02.

nodes.title: The reward is the after-cost portfolio return, minus a penalty on realized variance whose weight is a setting.

criteria: Given a day's return, cost and variance penalty weight, when the reward is computed, then it equals the return minus the cost minus the weighted penalty.

nodes.title: PPO is built from basic array and automatic-differentiation operations. No ready-made reinforcement-learning components are used.

criteria: Given the clipped policy loss on a hand-worked batch, when computed, then it matches the hand calculation within 1e-6.

nodes.title: The hand-built agent is checked against an established reference PPO implementation, on a standard control benchmark task and on the backtest environment.

criteria: Given 5 seeds each, when both are trained with the same budget, then the hand-built agent's median final return is ≥ 90% of the reference's on each task.

nodes.title: The agent is trained only on development-period walk-forward training windows, and scored on the following out-of-sample windows.

criteria: Given a scoring window, when the agent is scored, then none of its training episodes came from that window or later.

nodes.title: Agent results are reported as the median and range across at least 5 seeds.

criteria: Given a completed agent evaluation, when results are shown, then each metric has a median and a range across the seeds.

nodes.title: The agent "beats the classical portfolios" only under the same tests as FPORT-03 and FPORT-04, using its median seed. It must also beat the forecast portfolios on after-cost Sharpe, tested the same way.

criteria: Given an agent that beats S2 but not the forecast portfolios, when the verdict is recorded, then it says it beats S2 but not the forecast portfolios.

nodes.title: Only frozen strategy versions are paper traded: settings, trained weights and code version are fixed at start.

criteria: Given a running paper session, when any part of a strategy changes, then it counts as a new version and starts a new session.

nodes.title: After each close D, the system makes orders for D+1 from data up to D, and records them with a timestamp before D+1's prices are loaded.

criteria: Given an order record, when checked, then its timestamp is earlier than the loading of the price used to fill it.

nodes.title: Orders are filled at the close of D+1 under the cost model, and the fills are recorded.

criteria: Given an order, when it is filled, then the fill price is D+1's close and the cost is 10 bps per side.

nodes.title: Every S2 portfolio is paper traded alongside the candidates, over the same days.

criteria: Given a paper session for a candidate, when the session is read, then the S2 portfolios have records for the same days.

nodes.title: A paper test counts toward a verdict only after at least 63 trading days (about 3 months). The pass is directional, with no significance test deciding it. It passes only if, over the same days, the candidate's after-cost Sharpe ratio is higher than every S2 portfolio's, and its realized variance is lower than that of risk parity, HRP and equal weight. The minimum-variance comparison has no directional form, so it is decided only by the walk-forward and holdout tests (FPORT-03). The null-hypothesis-testing skill is also run on the same comparisons. Its p-values are reported for information only and do not change the pass or fail.

criteria: Given 63 or more days where the candidate meets every directional condition, when the p-values are not significant, then the paper test still passes.
Given 40 trading days of paper results, when a verdict is requested, then the answer is "not enough days yet".

nodes.title: The paper-trading log can only be added to, never changed.

criteria: Given a recorded order or fill, when an edit is attempted, then it is refused.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume, from 2005-01-03 to the latest close. It covers every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time in that range, plus 3 years before each stock entered the index.

criteria: Given the full dataset, when the stored range is checked, then it starts on or before 2005-01-03 for stocks that were members then, and ends at the latest close.

nodes.title: Point-in-time S&P 500 membership with effective entry and exit dates, including all former members.

criteria: Given any date in the range, when membership is rebuilt, then it meets UNIV-01 and UNIV-02.

nodes.title: Prices for stocks that were later delisted, acquired or removed, up to their last trading day.

criteria: Given the former members that stopped trading during the range, when their histories are checked, then at least 95% have prices up to within 5 trading days of their last trading day. The rest are listed by name.

nodes.title: Splits and dividends with ex-dates, and ticker changes with their dates.

criteria: Given 10 known splits and 10 known dividends, when they are checked against the store, then all 20 are present with correct dates and amounts.

nodes.title: All data sources together cost at most $50 a month.

criteria: Given the chosen sources, when costs are summed, then the total is ≤ $50 a month.

nodes.title: The data's terms of use allow personal research use and local storage.

criteria: Given each source, when its terms are checked, then personal research and local storage are allowed.

nodes.title: A full ingest runs on the laptop in at most 6 hours, apart from waits the source imposes, which are reported separately.

criteria: Timed on a full run, with the run record showing both durations.

nodes.title: A daily update run finishes in at most 10 minutes.

criteria: Timed on an update covering 1 to 5 new trading days.

nodes.title: Loading the full development-period total-return panel for all members takes at most 10 seconds.

criteria: Timed on the laptop with a warm start.

nodes.title: App views load in at most 2 seconds, and a stock's history chart in at most 1 second.

criteria: Timed in the browser on the laptop.

nodes.title: Live progress reaches the browser within 2 seconds of the change it reports.

criteria: Checked by comparing each progress event's timestamp with its display time during a run.

nodes.title: A full S2 walk-forward run covering all 10 portfolio–estimator pairs finishes in at most 1 hour on the laptop.

criteria: Timed on a run at the default window length.

nodes.title: The whole stored dataset uses at most 20 GB of disk.

criteria: Measured after a full ingest.

nodes.title: Any neural training run that needs a rented GPU costs at most $10.

criteria: Checked from the rental bill for the run, recorded in the run log.

attrs.trigger: qrp data full|update|validate on the command line, or "start run" in the app
the researcher opens a view in the app
qrp paper step, run by hand after each qrp data update

nodes.title: Trust every result. Nothing uses information from after its date, companies that left the index stay in, and no claim counts until it beats chance.
Judge every method against simpler baselines on the same unseen data and trading costs. A complex method must beat every simpler one.
Get risk right before predicting returns. Know which correlations between stocks are real and which are noise.
See the data and results in a browser, including long download and checking runs as they happen.
The system returns the S&P 500 membership as of any trading day from 2005-01-03 to the latest close.

criteria: Given a date D, when membership is requested, then the stocks returned are exactly those that were members at the close of D.
Given any trading day in the range, when membership is counted, then the count is between 495 and 510.
Given 10 dates spread across the range, when membership is compared with published index lists for those dates, then every difference is listed and explained. Unexplained differences: 0.

nodes.title: Each stock has a permanent identity across ticker changes.

criteria: Given a stock that changed its ticker, when its history is requested under either ticker, then one continuous history is returned under one identity.

nodes.title: Every entry to and exit from the index is listed with its effective date.

criteria: Given a date range, when changes are requested, then each entry and exit in the range is returned with stock, date and direction.

nodes.title: A full run downloads daily open, high, low, close and volume for every stock that was a member at any point since 2005-01-03, covering its membership period plus the 3 years before it entered.

criteria: Given an empty store, when a full run completes, then every past and present member has daily rows covering its membership period, apart from what is flagged under VAL.

nodes.title: The system stores splits and dividends, each with its ex-date and amount or ratio.

criteria: Given a stock with a known split, when its corporate actions are requested, then the split appears with its ex-date and ratio.

nodes.title: The system computes daily price returns and total returns from the stored prices and corporate actions.

criteria: Given a day with a 2-for-1 split and no price move, when returns are computed, then the price return and the total return are both 0 (within 1e-9).

Given a stock paying a dividend of 1% of the price on its ex-date, with the close otherwise unchanged, when returns are computed, then the total return is 1% higher than the price return (within 1e-6).

nodes.title: A stock's final return before delisting is kept.

criteria: Given a stock that stopped trading, when its returns are requested, then the history runs up to its last trading day, and the move to the final price is included.

nodes.title: An update run adds only the new trading days since the last stored close.

criteria: Given a store complete to day D, when an update runs on day D+5, then only days D+1 to D+5 are downloaded, and earlier stored rows are unchanged unless the source corrected them.
Given a run interrupted part-way, when it is started again, then it continues from the last completed stock, and the final store is identical to one produced by an uninterrupted run.

nodes.title: Every run records what it did.

criteria: Given a completed run, when its record is opened, then it shows start and end time, stocks attempted, stocks succeeded, stocks failed with reasons, and rows added or changed.

nodes.title: The system flags each member-day with no price row.

criteria: Given a member that is missing a trading day while a member, when validation runs, then that stock-day is flagged as "missing".

nodes.title: The system flags non-positive prices and inconsistent bars: high below low, or close outside the high–low range.

criteria: Given a row with high < low, when validation runs, then it is flagged as "inconsistent bar".

nodes.title: The system flags large moves with no corporate action to explain them: an absolute daily price return above 40%, with no split on that day.

criteria: Given a +60% price return with no split, when validation runs, then it is flagged as "unexplained jump".
Given a −50% price return on a 2-for-1 split's ex-date, when validation runs, then it is not flagged.

nodes.title: The system flags stale prices: 5 or more trading days in a row with an identical close and zero volume.

criteria: Given 5 such days, when validation runs, then each of the 5 is flagged as "stale".

nodes.title: The system flags duplicate rows for the same stock and day.

criteria: Given two rows for one stock-day, when validation runs, then both are flagged as "duplicate".

nodes.title: Flagged data is stored, never deleted.

criteria: Given flagged rows, when the store is read, then the rows are still present, each carrying its flag types.

nodes.title: Each validation run produces a report.

criteria: Given a run, when the report is opened, then it shows counts by flag type, by stock and by year, and the overall share of member-days that are flagged.

nodes.title: The share of member-days that are missing or flagged is at most 0.5% across the whole dataset.

criteria: Given the full dataset, when the validation report is produced, then the flagged share is ≤ 0.5%. If it is higher, the report lists the stocks that contribute the most.

nodes.title: Every request carries an as-of date, and nothing dated after it is returned.

criteria: Given as-of date D, when prices, returns, volume, corporate actions or membership are requested, then no value dated after D is returned.

nodes.title: The loader returns a panel of returns for the universe as of each day. A stock appears only on days it was a member, unless history before entry is requested.

criteria: Given a range, when a member-only returns panel is requested, then a stock's returns are present only on days it was a member.
Given a request for 3 years of history before each stock's entry, when the panel is returned, then that earlier history is included and marked as before entry.

nodes.title: Flagged data is left out by default and can be included on request.

criteria: Given a flagged stock-day, when data is loaded with default settings, then that value is missing in the result. When flagged data is requested, it is present, with its flags.

nodes.title: The loader returns either total returns or price returns, as requested.

criteria: Given a dividend day, when total and price returns are both requested, then they differ by the dividend yield.

nodes.title: Requests that touch the locked holdout are refused outside final-evaluation mode (see EVAL-06).

criteria: Given the holdout is locked, when a normal request covers any holdout day, then it fails with an error naming the holdout start date.

nodes.title: The analysis is run with the data-analysis skill on the development period of the dataset. It is given daily total returns, membership and the validation flags.

criteria: Given the dataset, when the analysis runs, then the report covers: summary statistics of returns, distribution and tail shape, missingness by stock and year, membership turnover per year, the average pairwise correlation over time, and the eigenvalue spectrum of the correlation matrix.

nodes.title: The report states the share of variance explained by the top eigenvalue in each calendar year.

criteria: Given the report, when the yearly table is read, then each year from 2005 on has one value.

nodes.title: Each finding in the report names the period and the stocks it was measured on.

criteria: Given any figure in the report, when it is read, then its caption states its date range and universe.

nodes.title: The app shows universe membership over time: the member count per day, and entries and exits per month.

criteria: Given the app is open, when the universe view loads, then the membership count is plotted from 2005-01-03 to the latest close.

nodes.title: The app shows any stock's history: price, total-return index, volume, corporate-action markers, flagged days and membership periods.

criteria: Given a stock, when it is chosen by ticker or name, past tickers included, then its history chart loads with splits, dividends, flags and membership periods marked.

nodes.title: The app lists validation flags, filterable by type, stock and year.

criteria: Given the flags view, when a filter is set to "unexplained jump" and the year 2008, then only matching flags are listed. Each one links to that stock's chart on that day.

nodes.title: The app shows the data-coverage picture: the share of member-days present, by year and by stock.

criteria: Given the coverage view, when it loads, then the coverage by year is shown and the stocks with the lowest coverage are listed.

nodes.title: The app shows the EDA report's figures and tables.

criteria: Given a completed EDA run, when the EDA view is opened, then its figures and tables are shown, with their captions.

nodes.title: The researcher can start a full ingest, an update or a validation run from the app.

criteria: Given no run in progress, when "update" is started, then a run begins and its live progress view opens.
Given a run already in progress, when another is started, then it is refused with "a run is already in progress".

nodes.title: Live progress of ingest and validation runs is pushed to the browser as it happens, without reloading. Progress shows the run type, phase, stocks done out of total, the current stock, failures so far and the estimated time remaining.

criteria: Given a running ingest, when progress changes, then the view updates within 2 seconds of the change.
Given a run started from the command line, when the app is open, then the same live progress is shown.

nodes.title: Live progress survives a page reload, and a finished run shows its summary.

criteria: Given a run in progress, when the page is reloaded, then progress resumes showing the current state within 2 seconds.
Given a run that has finished, when the view is open, then it shows the run record (ING-07) or the validation report (VAL-07).

nodes.title: (S2) The app shows the eigenvalue spectrum next to the random-matrix noise band, per window, and the out-of-sample comparisons of covariance estimators and portfolios.

criteria: Given a completed S2 evaluation, when its view is opened, then the spectrum, the realized-variance comparison table and the cumulative return curves are shown.

nodes.title: (S3) The app shows each feature's test result: information gain, p-value, corrected verdict, and the horizon it was tested at.

criteria: Given a completed S3 test run, when its view is opened, then every tested feature is listed, those that failed included.

nodes.title: (S4) The app shows forecasts against baselines, portfolio and agent return curves after costs, and the paper-trading log.

criteria: Given a completed S4 evaluation, when its view is opened, then the loss comparison against baselines and the after-cost Sharpe and variance comparison against S2 portfolios are shown.
Given paper trading is running, when its view is opened, then each day's orders, fills and running results are listed.

nodes.title: Factors are fitted only on returns inside the estimation window that ends at the decision date.

criteria: Given a window ending at D, when factors are fitted, then changing any return after D leaves the factors, loadings and residuals for days up to D unchanged.

nodes.title: The number of factors kept equals the number of correlation eigenvalues above the Marchenko–Pastur upper edge for that window's shape, unless a fixed number is requested.

criteria: Given a window, when factors are chosen, then the count and the noise edge are recorded with the window.

nodes.title: The system returns residual returns: each stock's return minus its exposure to the kept factors.

criteria: Given residual returns for a window, when their correlation matrix is computed, then the mean absolute off-diagonal correlation is lower than that of the raw returns.

nodes.title: The method recovers a planted structure.

criteria: Given simulated returns with 1 planted market factor plus 2 planted sector factors, 500 stocks and 756 days, when factors are fitted, then 3 factors are kept, and each planted loading vector correlates ≥ 0.95 with a recovered one.

nodes.title: Out-of-sample residuals are produced for later stages. Exposures fitted on a window are applied to the returns of the following holding period.

criteria: Given a window ending at D, when residuals for D+1 to the next rebalance are requested, then they use exposures fitted only on data up to D.

nodes.title: The system produces a sample covariance estimate per window.

criteria: Given a window with T days and N stocks, when the estimate is made, then it is symmetric and matches a direct calculation within 1e-10.

nodes.title: The system produces a shrinkage estimate that pulls the sample covariance toward a structured target, with the shrinkage amount estimated from the data.

criteria: Given a window, when the shrinkage estimate is made, then the shrinkage amount (between 0 and 1) is recorded, and the estimate is positive definite.

nodes.title: The system produces a denoised estimate. Correlation eigenvalues inside the Marchenko–Pastur noise band are replaced by their average, keeping the trace. The result is then turned back into a covariance.

criteria: Given a window, when the denoised estimate is made, then eigenvalues above the edge are unchanged, the trace of the correlation matrix equals N within 1e-8, and the estimate is positive definite.
Given simulated pure-noise returns, when denoised, then the denoised correlation matrix is closer to the identity (smaller Frobenius distance) than the sample one.

nodes.title: The estimation window length defaults to 756 trading days, and 504 and 1260 can also be chosen.

criteria: Given a window length setting, when estimates are made, then each window uses exactly that many trading days.

nodes.title: The estimators are compared on real data with the data-analysis skill. It is given each estimator's out-of-sample minimum-variance portfolio variance per rebalance, and its out-of-sample covariance forecast error per window, over the development period.

criteria: Given a completed S2 walk-forward run, when the comparison runs, then the report shows each estimator's realized variance and forecast error, with the spread over time and its stability across sub-periods (2005–2009, 2010–2014, 2015–2019, 2020 to the holdout start).

nodes.title: Any claim that one estimator beats another is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given the paired per-rebalance realized-variance differences over the development period. The claim passes only if the null of no difference is rejected at 5%, after correction for all estimator pairs compared.

criteria: Given the claim "denoised beats sample", when tested, then the report states the test, the p-value, the corrected verdict and the effect size.

nodes.title: At each rebalance date D, a strategy sees only data available as of D (through the loader, LOAD-01).

criteria: Given a strategy that tries to read data after D, when the run reaches D, then the read is refused and the run stops with an error.

nodes.title: Trades are filled at the close of D+1, and costs are charged at 10 bps per side on traded value.

criteria: Given a move from 100% cash to 100% in one stock, when the trade is filled, then the cost charged is 0.10% of the traded value.

nodes.title: Every result is reported both at the base cost and at 2× cost.

criteria: Given a completed run, when results are shown, then both cost levels are shown side by side.

nodes.title: A held stock that leaves the index stays held until the next rebalance. A held stock that stops trading takes its final return, and the proceeds move to cash.

criteria: Given a holding delisted mid-month, when the month is evaluated, then its final return is included, and its weight is cash until the next rebalance.

nodes.title: Training data for any fitted model is purged. No training sample's target window overlaps the period being scored, and an embargo of at least the longest target horizon separates them.

criteria: Given 21-day targets and a scoring period starting at day S, when training samples are chosen, then none has a target window reaching day S or later, and none starts within 21 trading days before S.

nodes.title: The locked holdout is used only in final-evaluation mode. Each strategy can be run on it once per version, and every holdout run is recorded.

criteria: Given a strategy version already evaluated on the holdout, when a second holdout run is asked for, then it is refused and the first result is shown.

nodes.title: Results include: annualized return, volatility, realized variance, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown and turnover, after costs, per run and per sub-period.

criteria: Given a completed run, when results are shown, then each of these metrics is shown at both cost levels.

nodes.title: Every evaluation run is logged with the strategy, its settings, the data range, the code version and the result. Failed and discarded runs are logged too.

criteria: Given any run, when the log is opened, then the run appears, and the log entry cannot be edited afterwards.
Given the same data, settings, code version and random seed, when a run is repeated, then all reported metrics are identical.

nodes.title: All classical portfolios are long-only, fully invested and unlevered.

criteria: Given any portfolio's weights, when checked, then every weight is ≥ 0 and the weights sum to 1 within 1e-8.

nodes.title: The minimum-variance portfolio minimizes the estimated variance under PORT-01.

criteria: Given a 3-stock covariance with a known solution, when solved, then the weights match it within 1e-6.

nodes.title: The risk parity portfolio gives each stock an equal share of the estimated portfolio variance.

criteria: Given any estimate, when solved, then every stock's share of risk is within 1% (relative) of 1/N.

nodes.title: The hierarchical risk parity portfolio clusters stocks by correlation, then splits weight top-down by cluster variance.

criteria: Given a covariance made of 2 uncorrelated blocks with equal block variance, when solved, then each block receives 50% of the weight within 1e-6.

nodes.title: An equal-weight portfolio of the universe is run as the baseline.

criteria: Given a rebalance date, when equal weight is built, then each eligible stock gets 1/N.

nodes.title: Each portfolio method is run on each covariance estimator (COV-01 to COV-03), giving one walk-forward result per pair.

criteria: Given a completed S2 run, when results are listed, then there are 3 methods × 3 estimators + equal weight = 10 results.

nodes.title: Portfolios are compared on out-of-sample realized variance, with the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given paired per-rebalance realized-variance differences between each portfolio and equal weight, and between portfolio methods, over the development period. A "lower variance" claim passes only if the null is rejected at 5% after correction for all comparisons made, at both cost levels.

criteria: Given the claim "denoised minimum-variance has lower realized variance than equal weight", when tested, then the report states the p-value, the corrected verdict and the variance ratio.

nodes.title: The S2 portfolios' holdout results (EVAL-06) are recorded once. They are the benchmarks for S4.

criteria: Given the S2 final evaluation, when run, then each portfolio's holdout metrics are stored, and S4 comparisons read these stored values.

nodes.title: Each feature is computed only from prices, volume, returns and corporate actions dated on or before its day.

criteria: Given a feature value for day D, when all data after D is removed and the feature is recomputed, then the value is unchanged.

nodes.title: Each feature is registered with a name, a plain-language definition, its lookback length and the date it was added.

criteria: Given the registry, when it is listed, then every feature shows these four fields.

nodes.title: The first candidate set covers at least these families: past-return momentum at several lookbacks, short-term reversal, realized volatility, volume and turnover change, and price range or liquidity measures.

criteria: Given the registry, when the S3 test run starts, then each family has at least one feature.

nodes.title: Features can be computed on raw returns or on residual returns (FACT-05).

criteria: Given a momentum feature, when the residual version is requested, then it uses out-of-sample residuals only.

nodes.title: Targets are the forward residual returns over 1, 5 and 21 trading days, built from out-of-sample residuals (FACT-05).

criteria: Given a stock on day D, when its 5-day target is built, then it covers days D+1 to D+5, with residuals that use exposures fitted only up to D.

nodes.title: A target is kept for a stock that leaves the index or stops trading during its window. It is computed up to the last trading day, never dropped.

criteria: Given a stock delisted on D+3, when its 5-day target is built, then the target includes returns through its final day.

nodes.title: Information gain is the out-of-sample improvement in prediction error of a learned model given the feature, compared with the same model without it. It is measured on walk-forward, purged and embargoed splits (EVAL-05) within the development period.

criteria: Given a feature and a horizon, when tested, then the report shows the error with and without the feature on every walk-forward fold.

nodes.title: Each feature at each horizon is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given the per-fold information gains, and builds a null by breaking the link between the feature and the target in time order. The feature survives only if the null of no gain is rejected at 5%, after correction across every feature-horizon pair ever tested in S3 (from the log, EVAL-08).

criteria: Given a feature made of random noise, when tested, then it does not survive.
Given a simulated feature with a planted link to the target, when tested, then it survives.

nodes.title: The set of surviving features, with their horizons, is recorded as the S3 verdict.

criteria: Given a completed S3 run, when the verdict is read, then it lists the survivors, or says "none survived".

nodes.title: S4 starts only from a recorded S3 verdict with at least one survivor.

criteria: Given the verdict "none survived", when an S4 forecasting run is started, then it refuses with "no surviving features from S3".

nodes.title: Return forecasts are made at the horizons where S3 features survived. Volatility forecasts are made at 1, 5 and 21 days.

criteria: Given an S3 verdict with survivors at 5 days only, when return forecasting is set up, then return forecasts are made at 5 days only.

nodes.title: Inputs on day D use only data up to D. Inputs include only the surviving features, plus past returns and past volatility.

criteria: Given a forecast for day D, when all data after D is removed and the forecast is remade, then it is unchanged.

nodes.title: Forecasting models are built from basic array and automatic-differentiation operations. No ready-made model components are used.

criteria: Given each model's layer, when its gradients are compared with numerical differences on a small input, then they agree within 1e-5 (relative).

nodes.title: The hand-built model is checked against an established reference implementation of the same model on the same data and settings.

criteria: Given the same data, settings and seed, when both are trained, then the hand-built model's validation loss is within 5% of the reference's.

nodes.title: Return forecasts are compared with baselines on out-of-sample walk-forward folds in the development period. The baselines are: a forecast of zero, the trailing mean, and a linear model on the same inputs.

criteria: Given a completed forecasting run, when results are shown, then each horizon shows the out-of-sample loss and the rank correlation with outcomes, for the model and for each baseline.

nodes.title: Volatility forecasts are compared with baselines out of sample: trailing realized volatility, an exponentially weighted average of squared returns, and a standard autoregressive volatility model.

criteria: Given a completed run, when results are shown, then each horizon shows the loss for the model and for each baseline.

nodes.title: A forecaster is said to "beat" its baselines only if the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given paired per-fold loss differences against the best baseline, rejects the null of equal loss at 5% after correction across horizons and targets.

criteria: Given a forecaster no better than the trailing mean, when tested, then the verdict is "does not beat".

nodes.title: Training on a rented GPU is optional. Every model can also be trained on the laptop alone, and results are reproducible from a seed either way.

criteria: Given the same seed and data, when a model is trained twice on the same hardware, then the forecasts match within 1e-6.

nodes.title: At each rebalance, weights are set from return forecasts, volatility forecasts and the best S2 covariance estimate, all as of the rebalance date. The weights are long-only, fully invested and unlevered.

criteria: Given a rebalance date, when weights are built, then they satisfy PORT-01 and use only forecasts made with data up to that date.

nodes.title: A turnover limit is applied so costs do not dominate: one-way turnover is at most 50% per rebalance.

criteria: Given earlier and new target weights, when the trade is made, then one-way turnover is ≤ 50%.

nodes.title: A forecast portfolio "beats the classical portfolios" only if all of these hold, each tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction across all comparisons:

criteria: its after-cost Sharpe ratio is higher than every S2 portfolio's (null of equal Sharpe rejected);
its realized variance is lower than that of the risk parity, hierarchical risk parity and equal-weight portfolios (null of equal variance rejected);
against each minimum-variance portfolio, its realized variance is not significantly higher (null of equal variance not rejected in the "higher" direction).

nodes.title: The final verdict also needs the paper-trading result (PAPER-05), which can veto a holdout pass but cannot replace one.

criteria: Given a holdout pass and a paper-trading fail, when the verdict is recorded, then it is "does not beat".
Given a holdout fail and a paper-trading pass, when the verdict is recorded, then it is "does not beat".

nodes.title: The environment's state at day D holds only information as of D: surviving features, forecasts, recent returns and current weights.

criteria: Given the environment at D, when the state is inspected, then no value is dated after D.

nodes.title: The agent's action is a set of target weights that meet PORT-01. Trades are filled at D+1 under the cost model (EVAL-02).

criteria: Given any action, when it is applied, then the weights are non-negative and sum to 1, and the cost charged follows EVAL-02.

nodes.title: The reward is the after-cost portfolio return, minus a penalty on realized variance whose weight is a setting.

criteria: Given a day's return, cost and variance penalty weight, when the reward is computed, then it equals the return minus the cost minus the weighted penalty.

nodes.title: PPO is built from basic array and automatic-differentiation operations. No ready-made reinforcement-learning components are used.

criteria: Given the clipped policy loss on a hand-worked batch, when computed, then it matches the hand calculation within 1e-6.

nodes.title: The hand-built agent is checked against an established reference PPO implementation, on a standard control benchmark task and on the backtest environment.

criteria: Given 5 seeds each, when both are trained with the same budget, then the hand-built agent's median final return is ≥ 90% of the reference's on each task.

nodes.title: The agent is trained only on development-period walk-forward training windows, and scored on the following out-of-sample windows.

criteria: Given a scoring window, when the agent is scored, then none of its training episodes came from that window or later.

nodes.title: Agent results are reported as the median and range across at least 5 seeds.

criteria: Given a completed agent evaluation, when results are shown, then each metric has a median and a range across the seeds.

nodes.title: The agent "beats the classical portfolios" only under the same tests as FPORT-03 and FPORT-04, using its median seed. It must also beat the forecast portfolios on after-cost Sharpe, tested the same way.

criteria: Given an agent that beats S2 but not the forecast portfolios, when the verdict is recorded, then it says it beats S2 but not the forecast portfolios.

nodes.title: Only frozen strategy versions are paper traded: settings, trained weights and code version are fixed at start.

criteria: Given a running paper session, when any part of a strategy changes, then it counts as a new version and starts a new session.

nodes.title: After each close D, the system makes orders for D+1 from data up to D, and records them with a timestamp before D+1's prices are loaded.

criteria: Given an order record, when checked, then its timestamp is earlier than the loading of the price used to fill it.

nodes.title: Orders are filled at the close of D+1 under the cost model, and the fills are recorded.

criteria: Given an order, when it is filled, then the fill price is D+1's close and the cost is 10 bps per side.

nodes.title: Every S2 portfolio is paper traded alongside the candidates, over the same days.

criteria: Given a paper session for a candidate, when the session is read, then the S2 portfolios have records for the same days.

nodes.title: A paper test counts toward a verdict only after at least 63 trading days (about 3 months). The pass is directional, with no significance test deciding it. It passes only if, over the same days, the candidate's after-cost Sharpe ratio is higher than every S2 portfolio's, and its realized variance is lower than that of risk parity, HRP and equal weight. The minimum-variance comparison has no directional form, so it is decided only by the walk-forward and holdout tests (FPORT-03). The null-hypothesis-testing skill is also run on the same comparisons. Its p-values are reported for information only and do not change the pass or fail.

criteria: Given 63 or more days where the candidate meets every directional condition, when the p-values are not significant, then the paper test still passes.
Given 40 trading days of paper results, when a verdict is requested, then the answer is "not enough days yet".

nodes.title: The paper-trading log can only be added to, never changed.

criteria: Given a recorded order or fill, when an edit is attempted, then it is refused.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume, from 2005-01-03 to the latest close. It covers every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time in that range, plus 3 years before each stock entered the index.

criteria: Given the full dataset, when the stored range is checked, then it starts on or before 2005-01-03 for stocks that were members then, and ends at the latest close.

nodes.title: Prices for stocks that were later delisted, acquired or removed, up to their last trading day.

criteria: Given the former members that stopped trading during the range, when their histories are checked, then at least 95% have prices up to within 5 trading days of their last trading day. The rest are listed by name.

nodes.title: Splits and dividends with ex-dates, and ticker changes with their dates.

nodes.title: Trust every result. Nothing uses information from after its date, companies that left the index stay in, and no claim counts until it beats chance.
Judge every method against simpler baselines on the same unseen data and trading costs. A complex method must beat every simpler one.
Get risk right before predicting returns. Know which correlations between stocks are real and which are noise.
See the data and results in a browser, including long download and checking runs as they happen.
The system returns the S&P 500 membership as of any trading day from 2005-01-03 to the latest close.

criteria: Given a date D, when membership is requested, then the stocks returned are exactly those that were members at the close of D.
Given any trading day in the range, when membership is counted, then the count is between 495 and 510.
Given 10 dates spread across the range, when membership is compared with published index lists for those dates, then every difference is listed and explained. Unexplained differences: 0.

nodes.title: Each stock has a permanent identity across ticker changes.

criteria: Given a stock that changed its ticker, when its history is requested under either ticker, then one continuous history is returned under one identity.

nodes.title: Every entry to and exit from the index is listed with its effective date.

criteria: Given a date range, when changes are requested, then each entry and exit in the range is returned with stock, date and direction.

nodes.title: A full run downloads daily open, high, low, close and volume for every stock that was a member at any point since 2005-01-03, covering its membership period plus the 3 years before it entered.

criteria: Given an empty store, when a full run completes, then every past and present member has daily rows covering its membership period, apart from what is flagged under VAL.

nodes.title: The system stores splits and dividends, each with its ex-date and amount or ratio.

criteria: Given a stock with a known split, when its corporate actions are requested, then the split appears with its ex-date and ratio.

nodes.title: The system computes daily price returns and total returns from the stored prices and corporate actions.

criteria: Given a day with a 2-for-1 split and no price move, when returns are computed, then the price return and the total return are both 0 (within 1e-9).

Given a stock paying a dividend of 1% of the price on its ex-date, with the close otherwise unchanged, when returns are computed, then the total return is 1% higher than the price return (within 1e-6).

nodes.title: A stock's final return before delisting is kept.

criteria: Given a stock that stopped trading, when its returns are requested, then the history runs up to its last trading day, and the move to the final price is included.

nodes.title: An update run adds only the new trading days since the last stored close.

criteria: Given a store complete to day D, when an update runs on day D+5, then only days D+1 to D+5 are downloaded, and earlier stored rows are unchanged unless the source corrected them.
Given a run interrupted part-way, when it is started again, then it continues from the last completed stock, and the final store is identical to one produced by an uninterrupted run.

nodes.title: Every run records what it did.

criteria: Given a completed run, when its record is opened, then it shows start and end time, stocks attempted, stocks succeeded, stocks failed with reasons, and rows added or changed.

nodes.title: The system flags each member-day with no price row.

criteria: Given a member that is missing a trading day while a member, when validation runs, then that stock-day is flagged as "missing".

nodes.title: The system flags non-positive prices and inconsistent bars: high below low, or close outside the high–low range.

criteria: Given a row with high < low, when validation runs, then it is flagged as "inconsistent bar".

nodes.title: The system flags large moves with no corporate action to explain them: an absolute daily price return above 40%, with no split on that day.

criteria: Given a +60% price return with no split, when validation runs, then it is flagged as "unexplained jump".
Given a −50% price return on a 2-for-1 split's ex-date, when validation runs, then it is not flagged.

nodes.title: The system flags stale prices: 5 or more trading days in a row with an identical close and zero volume.

criteria: Given 5 such days, when validation runs, then each of the 5 is flagged as "stale".

nodes.title: The system flags duplicate rows for the same stock and day.

criteria: Given two rows for one stock-day, when validation runs, then both are flagged as "duplicate".

nodes.title: Flagged data is stored, never deleted.

criteria: Given flagged rows, when the store is read, then the rows are still present, each carrying its flag types.

nodes.title: Each validation run produces a report.

criteria: Given a run, when the report is opened, then it shows counts by flag type, by stock and by year, and the overall share of member-days that are flagged.

nodes.title: The share of member-days that are missing or flagged is at most 0.5% across the whole dataset.

criteria: Given the full dataset, when the validation report is produced, then the flagged share is ≤ 0.5%. If it is higher, the report lists the stocks that contribute the most.

nodes.title: Every request carries an as-of date, and nothing dated after it is returned.

criteria: Given as-of date D, when prices, returns, volume, corporate actions or membership are requested, then no value dated after D is returned.

nodes.title: The loader returns a panel of returns for the universe as of each day. A stock appears only on days it was a member, unless history before entry is requested.

criteria: Given a range, when a member-only returns panel is requested, then a stock's returns are present only on days it was a member.
Given a request for 3 years of history before each stock's entry, when the panel is returned, then that earlier history is included and marked as before entry.

nodes.title: Flagged data is left out by default and can be included on request.

criteria: Given a flagged stock-day, when data is loaded with default settings, then that value is missing in the result. When flagged data is requested, it is present, with its flags.

nodes.title: The loader returns either total returns or price returns, as requested.

criteria: Given a dividend day, when total and price returns are both requested, then they differ by the dividend yield.

nodes.title: Requests that touch the locked holdout are refused outside final-evaluation mode (see EVAL-06).

criteria: Given the holdout is locked, when a normal request covers any holdout day, then it fails with an error naming the holdout start date.

nodes.title: The analysis is run with the data-analysis skill on the development period of the dataset. It is given daily total returns, membership and the validation flags.

criteria: Given the dataset, when the analysis runs, then the report covers: summary statistics of returns, distribution and tail shape, missingness by stock and year, membership turnover per year, the average pairwise correlation over time, and the eigenvalue spectrum of the correlation matrix.

nodes.title: The report states the share of variance explained by the top eigenvalue in each calendar year.

criteria: Given the report, when the yearly table is read, then each year from 2005 on has one value.

nodes.title: Each finding in the report names the period and the stocks it was measured on.

criteria: Given any figure in the report, when it is read, then its caption states its date range and universe.

nodes.title: The app shows universe membership over time: the member count per day, and entries and exits per month.

criteria: Given the app is open, when the universe view loads, then the membership count is plotted from 2005-01-03 to the latest close.

nodes.title: The app shows any stock's history: price, total-return index, volume, corporate-action markers, flagged days and membership periods.

criteria: Given a stock, when it is chosen by ticker or name, past tickers included, then its history chart loads with splits, dividends, flags and membership periods marked.

nodes.title: The app lists validation flags, filterable by type, stock and year.

criteria: Given the flags view, when a filter is set to "unexplained jump" and the year 2008, then only matching flags are listed. Each one links to that stock's chart on that day.

nodes.title: The app shows the data-coverage picture: the share of member-days present, by year and by stock.

criteria: Given the coverage view, when it loads, then the coverage by year is shown and the stocks with the lowest coverage are listed.

nodes.title: The app shows the EDA report's figures and tables.

criteria: Given a completed EDA run, when the EDA view is opened, then its figures and tables are shown, with their captions.

nodes.title: The researcher can start a full ingest, an update or a validation run from the app.

criteria: Given no run in progress, when "update" is started, then a run begins and its live progress view opens.
Given a run already in progress, when another is started, then it is refused with "a run is already in progress".

nodes.title: Live progress of ingest and validation runs is pushed to the browser as it happens, without reloading. Progress shows the run type, phase, stocks done out of total, the current stock, failures so far and the estimated time remaining.

criteria: Given a running ingest, when progress changes, then the view updates within 2 seconds of the change.
Given a run started from the command line, when the app is open, then the same live progress is shown.

nodes.title: Live progress survives a page reload, and a finished run shows its summary.

criteria: Given a run in progress, when the page is reloaded, then progress resumes showing the current state within 2 seconds.
Given a run that has finished, when the view is open, then it shows the run record (ING-07) or the validation report (VAL-07).

nodes.title: (S2) The app shows the eigenvalue spectrum next to the random-matrix noise band, per window, and the out-of-sample comparisons of covariance estimators and portfolios.

criteria: Given a completed S2 evaluation, when its view is opened, then the spectrum, the realized-variance comparison table and the cumulative return curves are shown.

nodes.title: (S3) The app shows each feature's test result: information gain, p-value, corrected verdict, and the horizon it was tested at.

criteria: Given a completed S3 test run, when its view is opened, then every tested feature is listed, those that failed included.

nodes.title: (S4) The app shows forecasts against baselines, portfolio and agent return curves after costs, and the paper-trading log.

criteria: Given a completed S4 evaluation, when its view is opened, then the loss comparison against baselines and the after-cost Sharpe and variance comparison against S2 portfolios are shown.
Given paper trading is running, when its view is opened, then each day's orders, fills and running results are listed.

nodes.title: Factors are fitted only on returns inside the estimation window that ends at the decision date.

criteria: Given a window ending at D, when factors are fitted, then changing any return after D leaves the factors, loadings and residuals for days up to D unchanged.

nodes.title: The number of factors kept equals the number of correlation eigenvalues above the Marchenko–Pastur upper edge for that window's shape, unless a fixed number is requested.

criteria: Given a window, when factors are chosen, then the count and the noise edge are recorded with the window.

nodes.title: The system returns residual returns: each stock's return minus its exposure to the kept factors.

criteria: Given residual returns for a window, when their correlation matrix is computed, then the mean absolute off-diagonal correlation is lower than that of the raw returns.

nodes.title: The method recovers a planted structure.

criteria: Given simulated returns with 1 planted market factor plus 2 planted sector factors, 500 stocks and 756 days, when factors are fitted, then 3 factors are kept, and each planted loading vector correlates ≥ 0.95 with a recovered one.

nodes.title: Out-of-sample residuals are produced for later stages. Exposures fitted on a window are applied to the returns of the following holding period.

criteria: Given a window ending at D, when residuals for D+1 to the next rebalance are requested, then they use exposures fitted only on data up to D.

nodes.title: The system produces a sample covariance estimate per window.

criteria: Given a window with T days and N stocks, when the estimate is made, then it is symmetric and matches a direct calculation within 1e-10.

nodes.title: The system produces a shrinkage estimate that pulls the sample covariance toward a structured target, with the shrinkage amount estimated from the data.

criteria: Given a window, when the shrinkage estimate is made, then the shrinkage amount (between 0 and 1) is recorded, and the estimate is positive definite.

nodes.title: The system produces a denoised estimate. Correlation eigenvalues inside the Marchenko–Pastur noise band are replaced by their average, keeping the trace. The result is then turned back into a covariance.

criteria: Given a window, when the denoised estimate is made, then eigenvalues above the edge are unchanged, the trace of the correlation matrix equals N within 1e-8, and the estimate is positive definite.
Given simulated pure-noise returns, when denoised, then the denoised correlation matrix is closer to the identity (smaller Frobenius distance) than the sample one.

nodes.title: The estimation window length defaults to 756 trading days, and 504 and 1260 can also be chosen.

criteria: Given a window length setting, when estimates are made, then each window uses exactly that many trading days.

nodes.title: The estimators are compared on real data with the data-analysis skill. It is given each estimator's out-of-sample minimum-variance portfolio variance per rebalance, and its out-of-sample covariance forecast error per window, over the development period.

criteria: Given a completed S2 walk-forward run, when the comparison runs, then the report shows each estimator's realized variance and forecast error, with the spread over time and its stability across sub-periods (2005–2009, 2010–2014, 2015–2019, 2020 to the holdout start).

nodes.title: Any claim that one estimator beats another is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given the paired per-rebalance realized-variance differences over the development period. The claim passes only if the null of no difference is rejected at 5%, after correction for all estimator pairs compared.

criteria: Given the claim "denoised beats sample", when tested, then the report states the test, the p-value, the corrected verdict and the effect size.

nodes.title: At each rebalance date D, a strategy sees only data available as of D (through the loader, LOAD-01).

criteria: Given a strategy that tries to read data after D, when the run reaches D, then the read is refused and the run stops with an error.

nodes.title: Trades are filled at the close of D+1, and costs are charged at 10 bps per side on traded value.

criteria: Given a move from 100% cash to 100% in one stock, when the trade is filled, then the cost charged is 0.10% of the traded value.

nodes.title: Every result is reported both at the base cost and at 2× cost.

criteria: Given a completed run, when results are shown, then both cost levels are shown side by side.

nodes.title: A held stock that leaves the index stays held until the next rebalance. A held stock that stops trading takes its final return, and the proceeds move to cash.

criteria: Given a holding delisted mid-month, when the month is evaluated, then its final return is included, and its weight is cash until the next rebalance.

nodes.title: Training data for any fitted model is purged. No training sample's target window overlaps the period being scored, and an embargo of at least the longest target horizon separates them.

criteria: Given 21-day targets and a scoring period starting at day S, when training samples are chosen, then none has a target window reaching day S or later, and none starts within 21 trading days before S.

nodes.title: The locked holdout is used only in final-evaluation mode. Each strategy can be run on it once per version, and every holdout run is recorded.

criteria: Given a strategy version already evaluated on the holdout, when a second holdout run is asked for, then it is refused and the first result is shown.

nodes.title: Results include: annualized return, volatility, realized variance, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown and turnover, after costs, per run and per sub-period.

criteria: Given a completed run, when results are shown, then each of these metrics is shown at both cost levels.

nodes.title: Every evaluation run is logged with the strategy, its settings, the data range, the code version and the result. Failed and discarded runs are logged too.

criteria: Given any run, when the log is opened, then the run appears, and the log entry cannot be edited afterwards.
Given the same data, settings, code version and random seed, when a run is repeated, then all reported metrics are identical.

nodes.title: All classical portfolios are long-only, fully invested and unlevered.

criteria: Given any portfolio's weights, when checked, then every weight is ≥ 0 and the weights sum to 1 within 1e-8.

nodes.title: The minimum-variance portfolio minimizes the estimated variance under PORT-01.

criteria: Given a 3-stock covariance with a known solution, when solved, then the weights match it within 1e-6.

nodes.title: The risk parity portfolio gives each stock an equal share of the estimated portfolio variance.

criteria: Given any estimate, when solved, then every stock's share of risk is within 1% (relative) of 1/N.

nodes.title: The hierarchical risk parity portfolio clusters stocks by correlation, then splits weight top-down by cluster variance.

criteria: Given a covariance made of 2 uncorrelated blocks with equal block variance, when solved, then each block receives 50% of the weight within 1e-6.

nodes.title: An equal-weight portfolio of the universe is run as the baseline.

criteria: Given a rebalance date, when equal weight is built, then each eligible stock gets 1/N.

nodes.title: Each portfolio method is run on each covariance estimator (COV-01 to COV-03), giving one walk-forward result per pair.

criteria: Given a completed S2 run, when results are listed, then there are 3 methods × 3 estimators + equal weight = 10 results.

nodes.title: Portfolios are compared on out-of-sample realized variance, with the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given paired per-rebalance realized-variance differences between each portfolio and equal weight, and between portfolio methods, over the development period. A "lower variance" claim passes only if the null is rejected at 5% after correction for all comparisons made, at both cost levels.

criteria: Given the claim "denoised minimum-variance has lower realized variance than equal weight", when tested, then the report states the p-value, the corrected verdict and the variance ratio.

nodes.title: The S2 portfolios' holdout results (EVAL-06) are recorded once. They are the benchmarks for S4.

criteria: Given the S2 final evaluation, when run, then each portfolio's holdout metrics are stored, and S4 comparisons read these stored values.

nodes.title: Each feature is computed only from prices, volume, returns and corporate actions dated on or before its day.

criteria: Given a feature value for day D, when all data after D is removed and the feature is recomputed, then the value is unchanged.

nodes.title: Each feature is registered with a name, a plain-language definition, its lookback length and the date it was added.

criteria: Given the registry, when it is listed, then every feature shows these four fields.

nodes.title: The first candidate set covers at least these families: past-return momentum at several lookbacks, short-term reversal, realized volatility, volume and turnover change, and price range or liquidity measures.

criteria: Given the registry, when the S3 test run starts, then each family has at least one feature.

nodes.title: Features can be computed on raw returns or on residual returns (FACT-05).

criteria: Given a momentum feature, when the residual version is requested, then it uses out-of-sample residuals only.

nodes.title: Targets are the forward residual returns over 1, 5 and 21 trading days, built from out-of-sample residuals (FACT-05).

criteria: Given a stock on day D, when its 5-day target is built, then it covers days D+1 to D+5, with residuals that use exposures fitted only up to D.

nodes.title: A target is kept for a stock that leaves the index or stops trading during its window. It is computed up to the last trading day, never dropped.

criteria: Given a stock delisted on D+3, when its 5-day target is built, then the target includes returns through its final day.

nodes.title: Information gain is the out-of-sample improvement in prediction error of a learned model given the feature, compared with the same model without it. It is measured on walk-forward, purged and embargoed splits (EVAL-05) within the development period.

criteria: Given a feature and a horizon, when tested, then the report shows the error with and without the feature on every walk-forward fold.

nodes.title: Each feature at each horizon is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given the per-fold information gains, and builds a null by breaking the link between the feature and the target in time order. The feature survives only if the null of no gain is rejected at 5%, after correction across every feature-horizon pair ever tested in S3 (from the log, EVAL-08).

criteria: Given a feature made of random noise, when tested, then it does not survive.
Given a simulated feature with a planted link to the target, when tested, then it survives.

nodes.title: The set of surviving features, with their horizons, is recorded as the S3 verdict.

criteria: Given a completed S3 run, when the verdict is read, then it lists the survivors, or says "none survived".

nodes.title: S4 starts only from a recorded S3 verdict with at least one survivor.

criteria: Given the verdict "none survived", when an S4 forecasting run is started, then it refuses with "no surviving features from S3".

nodes.title: Return forecasts are made at the horizons where S3 features survived. Volatility forecasts are made at 1, 5 and 21 days.

criteria: Given an S3 verdict with survivors at 5 days only, when return forecasting is set up, then return forecasts are made at 5 days only.

nodes.title: Inputs on day D use only data up to D. Inputs include only the surviving features, plus past returns and past volatility.

criteria: Given a forecast for day D, when all data after D is removed and the forecast is remade, then it is unchanged.

nodes.title: Forecasting models are built from basic array and automatic-differentiation operations. No ready-made model components are used.

criteria: Given each model's layer, when its gradients are compared with numerical differences on a small input, then they agree within 1e-5 (relative).

nodes.title: The hand-built model is checked against an established reference implementation of the same model on the same data and settings.

criteria: Given the same data, settings and seed, when both are trained, then the hand-built model's validation loss is within 5% of the reference's.

nodes.title: Return forecasts are compared with baselines on out-of-sample walk-forward folds in the development period. The baselines are: a forecast of zero, the trailing mean, and a linear model on the same inputs.

criteria: Given a completed forecasting run, when results are shown, then each horizon shows the out-of-sample loss and the rank correlation with outcomes, for the model and for each baseline.

nodes.title: Volatility forecasts are compared with baselines out of sample: trailing realized volatility, an exponentially weighted average of squared returns, and a standard autoregressive volatility model.

criteria: Given a completed run, when results are shown, then each horizon shows the loss for the model and for each baseline.

nodes.title: A forecaster is said to "beat" its baselines only if the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given paired per-fold loss differences against the best baseline, rejects the null of equal loss at 5% after correction across horizons and targets.

criteria: Given a forecaster no better than the trailing mean, when tested, then the verdict is "does not beat".

nodes.title: Training on a rented GPU is optional. Every model can also be trained on the laptop alone, and results are reproducible from a seed either way.

criteria: Given the same seed and data, when a model is trained twice on the same hardware, then the forecasts match within 1e-6.

nodes.title: At each rebalance, weights are set from return forecasts, volatility forecasts and the best S2 covariance estimate, all as of the rebalance date. The weights are long-only, fully invested and unlevered.

criteria: Given a rebalance date, when weights are built, then they satisfy PORT-01 and use only forecasts made with data up to that date.

nodes.title: A turnover limit is applied so costs do not dominate: one-way turnover is at most 50% per rebalance.

criteria: Given earlier and new target weights, when the trade is made, then one-way turnover is ≤ 50%.

nodes.title: A forecast portfolio "beats the classical portfolios" only if all of these hold, each tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5% after correction across all comparisons:

criteria: its after-cost Sharpe ratio is higher than every S2 portfolio's (null of equal Sharpe rejected);
its realized variance is lower than that of the risk parity, hierarchical risk parity and equal-weight portfolios (null of equal variance rejected);
against each minimum-variance portfolio, its realized variance is not significantly higher (null of equal variance not rejected in the "higher" direction).

nodes.title: The final verdict also needs the paper-trading result (PAPER-05), which can veto a holdout pass but cannot replace one.

criteria: Given a holdout pass and a paper-trading fail, when the verdict is recorded, then it is "does not beat".
Given a holdout fail and a paper-trading pass, when the verdict is recorded, then it is "does not beat".

nodes.title: The environment's state at day D holds only information as of D: surviving features, forecasts, recent returns and current weights.

criteria: Given the environment at D, when the state is inspected, then no value is dated after D.

nodes.title: The agent's action is a set of target weights that meet PORT-01. Trades are filled at D+1 under the cost model (EVAL-02).

criteria: Given any action, when it is applied, then the weights are non-negative and sum to 1, and the cost charged follows EVAL-02.

nodes.title: The reward is the after-cost portfolio return, minus a penalty on realized variance whose weight is a setting.

criteria: Given a day's return, cost and variance penalty weight, when the reward is computed, then it equals the return minus the cost minus the weighted penalty.

nodes.title: PPO is built from basic array and automatic-differentiation operations. No ready-made reinforcement-learning components are used.

criteria: Given the clipped policy loss on a hand-worked batch, when computed, then it matches the hand calculation within 1e-6.

nodes.title: The hand-built agent is checked against an established reference PPO implementation, on a standard control benchmark task and on the backtest environment.

criteria: Given 5 seeds each, when both are trained with the same budget, then the hand-built agent's median final return is ≥ 90% of the reference's on each task.

nodes.title: The agent is trained only on development-period walk-forward training windows, and scored on the following out-of-sample windows.

criteria: Given a scoring window, when the agent is scored, then none of its training episodes came from that window or later.

nodes.title: Agent results are reported as the median and range across at least 5 seeds.

criteria: Given a completed agent evaluation, when results are shown, then each metric has a median and a range across the seeds.

nodes.title: The agent "beats the classical portfolios" only under the same tests as FPORT-03 and FPORT-04, using its median seed. It must also beat the forecast portfolios on after-cost Sharpe, tested the same way.

criteria: Given an agent that beats S2 but not the forecast portfolios, when the verdict is recorded, then it says it beats S2 but not the forecast portfolios.

nodes.title: Only frozen strategy versions are paper traded: settings, trained weights and code version are fixed at start.

criteria: Given a running paper session, when any part of a strategy changes, then it counts as a new version and starts a new session.

nodes.title: After each close D, the system makes orders for D+1 from data up to D, and records them with a timestamp before D+1's prices are loaded.

criteria: Given an order record, when checked, then its timestamp is earlier than the loading of the price used to fill it.

nodes.title: Orders are filled at the close of D+1 under the cost model, and the fills are recorded.

criteria: Given an order, when it is filled, then the fill price is D+1's close and the cost is 10 bps per side.

nodes.title: Every S2 portfolio is paper traded alongside the candidates, over the same days.

criteria: Given a paper session for a candidate, when the session is read, then the S2 portfolios have records for the same days.

nodes.title: A paper test counts toward a verdict only after at least 63 trading days (about 3 months). The pass is directional, with no significance test deciding it. It passes only if, over the same days, the candidate's after-cost Sharpe ratio is higher than every S2 portfolio's, and its realized variance is lower than that of risk parity, HRP and equal weight. The minimum-variance comparison has no directional form, so it is decided only by the walk-forward and holdout tests (FPORT-03). The null-hypothesis-testing skill is also run on the same comparisons. Its p-values are reported for information only and do not change the pass or fail.

criteria: Given 63 or more days where the candidate meets every directional condition, when the p-values are not significant, then the paper test still passes.
Given 40 trading days of paper results, when a verdict is requested, then the answer is "not enough days yet".

nodes.title: The paper-trading log can only be added to, never changed.

criteria: Given a recorded order or fill, when an edit is attempted, then it is refused.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume, from 2005-01-03 to the latest close. It covers every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time in that range, plus 3 years before each stock entered the index.

criteria: Given the full dataset, when the stored range is checked, then it starts on or before 2005-01-03 for stocks that were members then, and ends at the latest close.

nodes.title: Point-in-time S&P 500 membership with effective entry and exit dates, including all former members.

criteria: Given any date in the range, when membership is rebuilt, then it meets UNIV-01 and UNIV-02.

nodes.title: Prices for stocks that were later delisted, acquired or removed, up to their last trading day.

criteria: Given the former members that stopped trading during the range, when their histories are checked, then at least 95% have prices up to within 5 trading days of their last trading day. The rest are listed by name.

nodes.title: Splits and dividends with ex-dates, and ticker changes with their dates.

criteria: Given 10 known splits and 10 known dividends, when they are checked against the store, then all 20 are present with correct dates and amounts.

nodes.title: All data sources together cost at most $50 a month.

criteria: Given the chosen sources, when costs are summed, then the total is ≤ $50 a month.

nodes.title: The data's terms of use allow personal research use and local storage.

criteria: Given each source, when its terms are checked, then personal research and local storage are allowed.

nodes.title: A full ingest runs on the laptop in at most 6 hours, apart from waits the source imposes, which are reported separately.

criteria: Timed on a full run, with the run record showing both durations.

nodes.title: A daily update run finishes in at most 10 minutes.

criteria: Timed on an update covering 1 to 5 new trading days.

nodes.title: Loading the full development-period total-return panel for all members takes at most 10 seconds.

criteria: Timed on the laptop with a warm start.

nodes.title: App views load in at most 2 seconds, and a stock's history chart in at most 1 second.

criteria: Timed in the browser on the laptop.

nodes.title: Live progress reaches the browser within 2 seconds of the change it reports.

criteria: Checked by comparing each progress event's timestamp with its display time during a run.

nodes.title: A full S2 walk-forward run covering all 10 portfolio–estimator pairs finishes in at most 1 hour on the laptop.

criteria: Timed on a run at the default window length.

nodes.title: The whole stored dataset uses at most 20 GB of disk.

criteria: Measured after a full ingest.

nodes.title: Any neural training run that needs a rented GPU costs at most $10.

criteria: Checked from the rental bill for the run, recorded in the run log.
